transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE); Jordan Park (Redwood CSM); Sophie Martin (NovaPay HoML); David Lee (NovaPay Infra); Marta Alvarez (NovaPay CTO); Tom Rivers (NovaPay SRE)

Summary:
Quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests; agree benchmark windows, go/no-go thresholds, required telemetry and reporting format; confirm timeline for pilot provisioning and data sharing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: ok everyone thanks for making time, um this is the sign-off call for the poc success criteria, i'll kick us off, quick agenda — review thresholds, bench plan, reporting outputs, and next steps.
[00:12] Sophie Martin: great, thanks. quick note, our goal is to validate both latency and quality under realistic payment auth loads — so there is a mix of short prompt classify flows and longer, multi-turn prompts for dispute triage.
[00:25] Priya Nambiar: perfect, Sophie. we prepared a draft acceptance doc, i can share screen but i'll just read the high level: 1) latency p95 under production mix must be <= 250ms for text-gen short flows (promptsize ~60 tokens); 2) throughput baseline of 120 req/s sustained on the dedicated pool for the mixed profile; 3) hallucination / incorrect action rate < 1% on a labeled eval set; 4) semantics accuracy (F1) >= 0.88 on the dispute triage dataset; 5) tail error rate (5xx) < 0.5% and no data leaks; and 6) cost per 1k tokens under target (we put $0.60 as placeholder).
[01:05] David Lee: couple questions — p95 250ms sounds aggressive, is that for hosted or dedicated? also the 120 req/s is assuming batch optimizations, what instance types are we using?
[01:18] Alex Chen: yeah good q — these thresholds are for Dedicated or Private deployments. for hosted we would expect slightly higher p95 but similar SLOs for premium tiers. for the benchmark we'll propose two sizing options: reserved x8 gpus (A100-80GB) for the high-throughput run, and a smaller q8 (like 4 x A10 or equivalent) to show cost tradeoffs. we'll attach the exact instance SKUs in the sizing sheet.
[01:40] Marta Alvarez: ok can we walk through acceptance test mechanics? like we need deterministic steps to reproduce and a pass/fail criteria.
[01:48] Priya Nambiar: absolutely. acceptance tests will be a 2-week window with three phases: Phase A (sanity, 1 day) — smoke tests on internal subset; Phase B (72 hour steady-state) — run customer traffic profile at target throughput; Phase C (24 hour stress + regression eval) — include failover scenarios and cold KV-cache runs. pass if all thresholds met in Phase B and no critical regression in Phase C. we will also run quality evals daily against the labeled set and track metrics.
[02:20] Tom Rivers: what do you mean by cold KV-cache runs? we need to simulate warm vs cold caches; in prod our tail latency spikes when caches are cold.
[02:28] Priya Nambiar: right — we'll schedule a cold-warm cycle where we flush prefix cache and re-run a subset to measure cold p95 and p99. cold p95 target is <= 450ms, cold p99 <= 900ms — these are documented in the draft.
[02:40] Sophie Martin: on quality, you mention hallucination <1% — how are you measuring hallucination? we have a labeled set where each response is scored yes/no for hallucination and annotated with severity.
[02:52] Priya Nambiar: we'll compute hallucination rate over the labeled set (binary) plus a weighted severity score. primary pass criteria is binary hallucination <1%; if it's slightly above we use severity to decide go/no-go.
[03:05] David Lee: ok for throughput, when you say 120 req/s sustained, is that concurrency or qps per model shard?
[03:11] Alex Chen: it's overall QPS to the service under the mixed workload. our runtime will autoscale within the dedicated pool but for the benchmark we'll fix instance count to measure unit economics. we'll provide per-node metrics as well so you can map to your capacity planning.
[03:26] Sophie Martin: reporting format — we need per-minute latency histograms, per-endpoint error counts, token counts, and a CSV export of raw traces for the 72-hour runs. can you provide dashboards too?
[03:38] Jordan Park: yes — we'll deliver: 1) a CSV with raw request/response rows (timestamp, route, latency_ms, status_code, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate, model_version), 2) aggregated dashboards in the Redwood Console with p50/p95/p99, per-route breakdown, and 3) a summary PDF with pass/fail and a short diagnostics section. we'll also include an artifacts bundle with model outputs for the labeled evals.
[04:05] Marta Alvarez: data residency — the logs in CSV contain request text, we need PII redaction and KMS encryption. are you able to mask or scrub request bodies?
[04:15] Alex Chen: yes, for the POC we can enable request masking for exports and use customer-managed KMS for any persisted artifacts. we'll note that in the security checklist and Jordan will share the SOC2/ISO docs.
[04:27] Tom Rivers: what about SSO and RBAC access to the dashboards? we need to lock down who can see raw traces.
[04:33] Jordan Park: SSO via SAML is supported; we can restrict exports and raw trace access to a small group. we'll include recommended RBAC roles in the deliverables.
[04:44] Sophie Martin: timeline — if we sign this, when can you start the benchmark? we are aiming for customer demo on 2025-08-25, so pilot results need to be in early August.
[04:54] Alex Chen: proposed timeline in doc: 1) NovaPay shares traffic profile & labeled corpus by 2025-07-25; 2) Redwood provisions dedicated pool and test harness by 2025-07-30; 3) run initial sanity and quick runs 2025-07-31 to 2025-08-02; 4) 72-hour steady-state window 2025-08-04 to 2025-08-07; 5) 24-hour stress + regression 2025-08-08; 6) analysis and go/no-go review week of 2025-08-11; final sign-off meeting 2025-08-21. does that fit your calendar?
[05:31] Sophie Martin: it does, though we may need the 72-hour window earlier — but seems workable.
[05:36] David Lee: small ask — can we see cost projections for both reserved and burst configs? we'd like a cost per 1k tokens and cost per 100k requests.
[05:45] Priya Nambiar: yes — the sizing sheet will include estimated cost delta for quantized vs FP16 runs and reserved vs burst. our Optimize team will add recommended quantization profile and expected quality delta.
[05:55] Marta Alvarez: acceptance criteria around regressions — if the labeled F1 drops by >0.03 vs baseline, is that an automatic fail?
[06:03] Priya Nambiar: baseline rule we proposed: absolute F1 decrease > 0.03 -> fail. but we also look at example-level regressions; if drop is concentrated on low-frequency intents we may accept with mitigations. we can tie the final decision to a joint review.
[06:20] Tom Rivers: do you capture model version hashes in reports? we need exact reproducibility.
[06:25] Alex Chen: yes every run will include model commit/hash, runtime kernel versions, and container image tags in the CSV metadata.
[06:33] Sophie Martin: ok i'm comfortable with this. a few clarifying points: 1) provide a single-pass template for the go/no-go decision (binary plus notes), 2) ensure SREs can run their own replay with your harness, 3) confirm the cost target we put was a placeholder — we'll finalize after you send spreadsheet.
[06:52] Priya Nambiar: will do. for the go/no-go template we'll include columns: metric, threshold, observed, pass/fail, notes. and we'll include link to raw artifacts.
[07:03] Alex Chen: great. last bit — backup plan if the dedicated pool isn't available: we can run the benchmark in Redwood hosted premium with slightly relaxed latency targets (p95 <= 350ms) and then run a smaller dedicated pass later.
[07:17] Marta Alvarez: acceptable as fallback.
[07:20] Sophie Martin: ok let's recap next steps verbally.
[07:24] Alex Chen: recap: 1) Redwood to send final pilot pricing + sizing (Alex) by 2025-07-23; 2) Redwood SE (Priya) to provision test harness and run initial sanity by 2025-07-30; 3) NovaPay to send traffic profile & labeled corpus (David/Sophie) by 2025-07-25; 4) security docs and SOC2 (Jordan) by 2025-07-24; 5) schedule benchmark window starting 2025-08-04; 6) go/no-go review meeting 2025-08-21.
[07:58] Sophie Martin: sounds good, thanks all.
[08:00] Alex Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the files and a calendar invite for the benchmark windows.

End of transcript.
